name: Bryn Shander
description: Largest of the Ten Towns and the hub of the knucklehead trade.

name: Luskan
description: The City of Sails, a port at the mouth of the River Mirar built over the ruins of Illusk. Five High Captains, each heading a pirate Ship, rule it; a free port since 1376 DR, it took up legal sea trade along the Sword Coast after 1485 DR while secretly under Jarlaxle and Bregan D'aerthe.

name: Neverwinter
description: The Jewel of the North, a Lords' Alliance port on the High Road between Waterdeep and Luskan. Its river, warmed beneath Mount Hotenow, keeps the harbour ice-free and the hothouse gardens green, and its crafters were famed for multicoloured glass lamps, water clocks and jewellery. Destroyed by the eruption of 1451 DR, it was rebuilt under Lord Protector Dagult Neverember, who reopened trade; by 1491 DR merchants were returning and a trading alliance with Gauntlgrym was forming, though ruins remained around the sealed Chasm.

name: Port Llast
description: Small town on the High Road north of Neverwinter, once Grath's Hold and Last Port and for a time capital of Stornanter. Known for skilled stonecutters, who work quarries on the coastal headlands just south of town, and for a harbour sheltered by a rocky spit; stone is its recorded export and twelve fishing boats worked the harbour circa 1365 DR, when about 700 people lived there. Ruled by a First Captain, allied with Neverwinter and a Lords' Alliance member, coveted by Luskan. Silting after 1385 DR and sahuagin and bandit raids emptied much of the town; districts were retaken and resettled in 1463 DR, and by the 1480s DR most residents were fishers. Frost giants raided it twice after 1486 DR.

name: Leilon
ruler: Town council loyal to Lord Protector Dagult Neverember

name: Phandalin
description: Rebuilt frontier village of farmers, woodcutters, trappers and prospectors in the Lost Hills of the Sword Mountains, south of Neverwinter Wood, resettled from about 1486 DR on the ruins of a 10th-century town. Gold and platinum mining bring most of its wealth; it also trades timber and skins. Edermath Orchard grows apples and makes cider, Barthen's Provisions is the main trading post, and the Miner's Exchange weighs and buys ore and keeps claim records.

name: Mirabar
description: Walled mining city on a knoll on the north bank of the River Mirar, called the richest city north of Waterdeep in 1368 DR. Shield dwarves work the mines and forges of the Undercity beneath it while humans move ore to market and defend it; roads lead to guarded mines in the Spine of the World. Cut stone and worked metal go by magically floating barges down the Mirar to Luskan and on south, ground minerals and gems colour its glazed pottery, and in 1491 DR it made its own iron trade bars worth 5 gp. A hereditary marchion (Elastul Raurym around 1368 to 1370 DR; Selin Ramur after 1485 DR, a member of the Lords' Alliance) handles foreign affairs, while the elected Council of Sparkling Stones sets mining quotas and trade terms; the Axe of Mirabar defends the city and mines. Population 23,000 in 1357 and 1370 DR and 10,307 in 1372 DR.

name: Longsaddle
description: Small hamlet on an isolated stretch of the Long Road between the Crags and the Evermoors, founded in 1042 DR by Shardra Harpell and home of the eccentric Harpell wizards of the Ivy Mansion. Ranchers graze the surrounding grassland; beef and mutton are its exports. About 130 lived in the village (1358 and 1366 DR) and some 1,100 in the surrounding area (1358 DR). Inns, festhalls, a horse trader, a stirrup and spur smithy and travellers' outfitters serve Long Road traffic. Governed by a council of elders led by the Harpells; Dowell Harpell spoke for it on the Lords' Alliance council in 1489 DR.

name: Triboar
description: Prosperous trading town and frontier crossroads where the Evermoor Way meets the Long Road in the Dessarin Valley, ruled by an elected Lord Protector. Known for wagons, caravan services and guides, horse and pony ranches west of town, cattle dealing, forged ironware and leather goods such as harness. About 2,500 people in the mid 14th century DR; by the late 15th century DR nearly half lived on outlying farms and ranches (Forgotten Realms Wiki, citing Volo's Guide to the North, The North and Storm King's Thunder).

name: Yartar
description: Fortified trading city on the east bank of the River Surbrin near its meeting with the Dessarin, where the Evermoor Way crosses by a fortified bridge to the Shield Tower citadel on the west bank. A crossroads for caravans and river barges between Waterdeep and Silverymoon, known for fishing (crab, eel and other catch sold in the Fishyard market) and barge-building; it imports food, with grain and produce from Goldenfields. Ruled by an elected Waterbaron; a Lords' Alliance member. Sources: Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide, pp. 57 to 58; Princes of the Apocalypse, pp. 33, 39; Volo's Guide to the North, pp. 93 to 96 (via the Forgotten Realms Wiki).

name: Red Larch
description: Waystop village on the Long Road about seven days' ride north of Waterdeep, on a low ridge at the western edge of the Dessarin Valley where trails lead to Bargewright Inn and Kheldell. Known for stone quarries in the hills to the east, harness-makers, wagonworks, a poultry farm and crumblecake, a baked loaf of nuts, chickpeas, roots and fowl.

name: Amphail
description: Village on the Long Road between Waterdeep and Red Larch. Grows food for Waterdeep and is renowned for its horses, bred by wealthy landowners and noble families.

name: Goldenfields
description: Walled abbey-farm of Chauntea, the Granary of the North, on raised ground on the western side of the River Dessarin, south of Bargewright Inn. Its farms, orchards and gardens grow grain, maize, rice, barley, hops, apples, oranges, herbs and vegetables, and it keeps cattle, oxen, sheep, pigs and poultry; much of its food goes to Waterdeep and nearby settlements, given in Chauntea's honour. The Goldengulp Brewery brews its namesake beer.

name: Waterdeep
ruler: Open Lord Laeral Silverhand and the Lords of Waterdeep
description: City of Splendors; the greatest market on the Sword Coast.

name: Daggerford
ruler: Duchess Morwen Daggerford (identity disputed in 1489 DR)
description: Walled farming town and duchy on the Trade Way, on the north bank of the Delimbiyr (the Shining River). Cargo moves here between river boats and Trade Way caravans, since the river is too shallow for ships further upstream. Exports furs and garments and imports timber; has river shipyards, smithies, a tannery outside the walls and a brewery. Ruled by a Duke or Duchess of the Daggerford line, with a Council of Guilds handling daily affairs.

name: Secomber
description: Small town on three stone hills on the north bank of the River Delimbiyr where the Unicorn Run joins it, built on the ruins of Hastarl, ancient capital of Athalantar; the High Moor lies to the south. A stop on the Delimbiyr Route between Daggerford and Loudwater, with the Secomber Trail north to Uluvin. Farming, fishing and stone-cutting are the main occupations, and locals hire out as guides and guards for caravans and adventurers. Mostly humans with nearly as many halflings, and some dwarves. Justice is kept by elected Rods of Justice and juries of landowners; a small Lords' Alliance garrison held a hilltop fort in the 14th century DR. By 1479 DR hobgoblin raids had forced the walled town to pay tribute, which later left it poor.

name: Baldur's Gate
description: Gateway city of the Chionthar and the Gate.

name: Candlekeep
description: Fortress-library of Oghma; admission costs a book of rare worth.

name: Scornubel
description: The Caravan City, where every road in the Heartlands crosses.

name: Berdusk
description: Jewel of the Vale, famed for Berduskan Dark.

name: Iriaebor
description: The City of a Thousand Spires.

name: Silverymoon
description: The Gem of the North, the largest city of the Interior North, split by the River Rauvin into the older walled Northbank and the Southbank, joined by the magical Moonbridge. A magocracy of the arts, music and magical study and seat of the Conclave of Silverymoon; it exports books, paper, inks, herbs, glassware, furs, timber and Silverymoon Blue wine, and imports food (especially grain and livestock), armor, weapons, footwear and clothing.

name: Everlund
description: Walled city of merchant traders and caravan companies, the second largest in the Silver Marches, on the north bank of the River Rauvin (which runs through the heart of the city) about 50 miles from Silverymoon, founded in 515 DR when settlers from Ascalhorn refurbished an old dwarf-keep at a Rauvin crossing. Two bridges (Knightbridge and Dwarfbridge) cross the river and five gates (Silverymoon, Mountain, Upriver, Bridge and Downriver) open from dawn to dusk, with straight streets running to the Bell Market at the centre. It is the eastern end of the Evermoor Way, which it keeps safe as far as Calling Horns, with roads to Silverymoon and a trail up the Rauvin to Sundabar; rapids block boats downstream, while the river is navigable about 170 miles upstream to Sundabar. Exports amber, charcoal, furniture, furs, stone, syrup, timber and valuable ores, and imports ale, armor, cheese, clothing, fruit, grain, sugar, weapons and wine (Silver Marches, 2002); the sweet wine evershimmer is also made there (Volo's Guide to the North, 1993). Population 21,388 in 1372 DR and about 23,000 in 1479 DR. Ruled by a Council of Six Elders led by a First Elder (High Captain Kayl Moorwalker in 1372 DR) and defended by the Army of the Vale; Moongleam Tower is a Harper base. In the late 1480s or early 1490s DR the council, then including High Captain Horix Zoar, voted 3 to 2 to leave the Lords' Alliance (Storm King's Thunder, pp. 81 to 82).

name: Sundabar
description: Fortress-city of the Vault of the Sages and dwarven forges.

name: Citadel Adbar
description: Impregnable dwarfhold of Clan Battlehammer's allies.

name: Mithral Hall
description: The mithral delve of Clan Battlehammer, richest forge in the North.

name: Nesmé
description: Walled frontier town beside the River Surbrin on the edge of the Evermoors, ruled by a First Speaker and dominated by its merchants. Almost all east and west trade passed through it, and it was known for its steel, exporting iron ore, steel weapons and armor (1371 DR). Ruined by trolls in 1370 DR and rebuilt larger with a double wall; overrun by the orcs of Many-Arrows in 1484 DR and still in ruins in 1485 DR.

name: Jalanthar
description: Hamlet of trappers and hunters on the River Rauvin in the Silver Marches, on the trail between Everlund and Sundabar near the southern end of the Moon Pass. Its turf-covered houses are dug into the hillsides against fire and battering. Residents trade furs and hire out as guides. Around 1372 DR, after repeated orc raids, it moved from the river's south bank to the foothills north of it, held 226 people under a council of elders, and hosted a company of the Argent Legion; a protectorate of Luruar without a vote. In the late 15th century DR a retired ranger, Quinn Nardrosz, headed the village council and Myles Heldruin kept the Crowing Cockatrice inn.

name: Evereska
description: The hidden elven refuge of the Vine Vale.

name: Menzoberranzan
description: City of Spiders; wealth flows in blood and obsidian.

name: Gracklstugh
description: The City of Blades, forge of the duergar.

name: Mantol-Derith
description: Neutral trading enclave where drow, duergar and svirfneblin deal.

name: Sshamath
description: The City of Dark Weavings, ruled by wizards rather than priestesses.

name: Athkatla
description: City of Coin: nothing happens in Amn without a fee.

name: Crimmor
description: Caravan capital and leatherworking heart of Amn.

name: Zazesspur
description: Tethyr's greatest port and shipyard.

name: Darromar
description: Royal capital of Tethyr.

name: Calimport
description: Vast, ancient and byzantine; the greatest bazaar in the South.

name: Port Nyanzaru
description: The only safe harbour in Chult, and it charges for it.

name: Halarahh
description: Wizard-ruled and skyship-served; magic here is a commodity.

name: Arrabar
description: Capital of Chondath and a primary port of the Vilhon Reach at the end of the Golden Road and the Emerald Way; trade, crafting, fishing and mercenary work. Destroyed in the Spellplague and back on the map by the late 15th century DR as a port stop on the Reach.

name: Westgate
description: The Gateway to the West, and the most corrupt port on the Inner Sea.

name: Suzail
description: Capital of the Forest Kingdom; the Purple Dragons buy well and pay well.

name: Marsember
description: Cormyr's smuggler-haunted seaport.

name: Arabel
description: Cormyr's caravan crossroads and garrison city.

name: Shadowdale
description: Small, storied, and watched over by mages.

name: Myth Drannor
description: The City of Song, reborn amid its ruins.

name: Selgaunt
description: Sembia's richest port: coin is the only creed.

name: Saerloon
description: Home of Saerloonian Glowfire wine.

name: Ravens Bluff
description: The Living City: chaotic, wealthy and litigious.

name: Melvaunt
description: Ironworks city of the northern Moonsea.

name: Mulmaster
description: City of Danger, ruled by the Blades and the Brotherhood.

name: Zhentil Keep
description: The Black Network's fortress-market.

name: Telflamm
description: Western terminus of the Golden Way from Kara-Tur.

name: Eltabbar
description: Thayan capital; magic is manufactured here at scale.

name: Bezantur
description: City of a Thousand Temples and Thay's great port.

name: Skuld
description: The City of Shadows, ancient seat of Mulhorandi divinity.

name: Caer Calidyrr
description: High King's seat on Alaron, granary of the Isles.

name: Mintarn
description: Island free port in the Sea of Swords, about 400 miles south-west of Waterdeep, ruled by a tyrant. A haven that asks no questions, welcoming fugitives, pirates and parties seeking neutral ground. Exports mercenaries (the White Sails company), ships and its own drink: golden Mintarn lager, cold green wine, almond brandy and whisky; rock salt is mined in the northern islands. Pays yearly tribute to the red dragon Hoondarrh of Skadaurak Island; Tyrant Bloeth Embuirhan ruled around 1489 DR.

name: Orlumbor
description: Small, rocky, barren island city-state in the Sea of Swords off the Sword Coast, west of the Trollbark Forest between Daggerford and Baldur's Gate and about 300 miles south of Waterdeep. The town is cut into the rock around a mainland-facing natural harbour, its cave-like buildings linked by tunnels and stairs; the harbour approach is treacherous. Its people are goat-herders, fishers and renowned shipwrights who build and repair many of the ocean-going ships of the North (small merchant vessels in about two months, large trade ships in six, warships in four or more). It exports fish, goats and ships and imports timber, the island having been logged bare by 1367 DR. Local families privately own the docks and warehouses. Independent under Waterdeep's patronage, allied with Baldur's Gate from 1364 DR, and a Lords' Alliance member circa 1491 DR.

name: Loudwater
description: Loudwater, the City of Grottos, is a walled garden town where the Grayflow joins the River Delimbiyr in the Gray Vale (Delimbiyr Vale). High Town on the north bank holds the High Lord's Hall and the old elven houses; Low Town on the south bank holds the markets, workshops, warehouses and a modest river harbour, joined by the dwarf-built Flying Fish Bridge. Its people farm, fish and serve the caravans and riverboats of the Delimbiyr Route, and the vale was known for rich cave-ripened cheeses such as mist cheese and for carved hardwoods. About 4,000 people lived there in 1357 to 1370 DR and 8,137 in 1372 DR; trade collapsed after the Spellplague, and by 1479 DR about 2,000 remained behind a stone and timber wall, where carts paid a 5 sp toll at the gates. In the late 1480s DR the wizard Telbor Zazrek ruled as High Lord, secretly a Zhentarim puppet; prices were high, goods not supplied by the Zhentarim were heavily taxed, and refugees from stone giant raids on Llorkh and Orlbar crowded the riverside warehouses.

description: Grandfather Tree is an arakhor (an elder treant) in the form of a gnarled oak over 350 feet tall, deep in the High Forest, summoned by the elves of Aryvandaar around -12,500 DR to guard the Hall of Mists beneath its roots. It is the sacred ancestral mound of the Uthgardt Tree Ghost tribe, which rediscovered it on Shieldmeet 1368 DR and founded the hamlet of Ghostand in the oaks nearby (224 to about 350 people in 1372 DR, mostly human with wood elves and half-elves), a trading place for forest folk in the late 14th century DR. Great Chief Boorvald Orcbane led the tribe around 1485 DR. The tree itself is a holy site, not a market; no trade goods are recorded.

name: Griffon's Nest
description: Permanent settlement of the Uthgardt Griffon tribe in the Surbrin Hills of the Savage Frontier, northeast of Longsaddle, with Shining Creek to the east. In the mid-14th century DR it was a palisaded village of thatched wood-and-earth huts around a longhouse and two warehouses, with hillside farms, trading woven rush goods, cane baskets and trunks for steel weapons under Chief Kralgar Bonesnapper. By 1485 DR it had declined to a poor, hostile hamlet of about 300 under Halric Bonesnapper that raided homesteads in the Dessarin Valley.

name: Warlock's Crypt
description: City of undead in the western Troll Hills on the Sword Coast, near the mouth of the Winding Water, built from the ruins of the Netherese flying enclave Orbedal (Sanctuary), which fell there in -339 DR. Also called Warlock's Keep, a corruption of Larloch's Crypt. Ruled by the lich Larloch, the Shadow King: about sixty liches by 1374 DR, with vampires, wraiths, wights and lesser undead, guarded by trolls and patrolled by bat-riding undead. Travelers are warned to stay out of sight of it. No living community, trade or market is recorded.
